lines.text: Oh, hello. Dot Lau. I look after the Dex round here.
Forty years painting shop signs in Deptford.
Birds fidget more than shopkeepers, but they don’t haggle.
Shall I show you round? Five minutes, and only a few drawings.
This is Explore. Every pin is a real birding spot near you.
The reports come from birders on eBird, so they’re days old, not years.
This card is today’s pick: {siteName}.
lines.fallback: This card is today’s pick: the best spot within your drive.

lines.text: {bird} was seen there {when}. It’s {minutes} minutes away.
lines.fallback: It tells you what’s been seen there lately, and how far it is.

lines.text: {newCount} birds there aren’t in your Dex yet. That’s the point of going.
lines.fallback: The more birds there you haven’t got, the higher it ranks.

lines.text: The coral pin is that spot on the map. The bird inside is the one worth the petrol.
Little pins are other spots with fresh reports. Tap one to swap.
A flag means a bird you’ve starred as a target has turned up there.
This one means you’ve not been yet. First visits count for extra.
And a gem means scarce round here. Gold’s the one you ring someone about.
How far will you drive? I take the bus myself, so I’ll trust you.
After one bird in particular? Find a bird searches every recent report for it.
Plan a day strings a few spots into one trip, then hands it to Google Maps.
And this is where the drive starts from. Tap it to change area.
Let’s look at a real one. Go on, tap View spot. I’ll wait.
Every bird seen there lately, with its date and checklist.
Those are other people’s sightings, mind.
They tell you where to look. They don’t go in your Dex.
This is your Dex. {recorded} of {dexSize} so far.
lines.fallback: This is your Dex: about a hundred birds you can find within a fair drive.

lines.text: Grey ones are still to find. I don’t hide the names.
Tap a bird for its page: where it’s been seen, and how well you know it.
Use eBird already? Bring your data in here and your Dex fills itself.
Or log a sighting yourself with this.
Only birds you’ve seen count. That’s the one rule I’m fussy about.
Folk is people. Wardens look after the big reserves and set you jobs.
That’s the lot. If you forget anything, I’m in Settings.
Off you go, then. Bring me something good.
